newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ electricity futures fail to trade on debut.
newsitem.headline: NZ electricity futures fail to trade on debut.

text.p: The world's first cash-settled electricity futures contract made a less than spectacular debut on the New Zealand Futures and Options Exchange on Monday, failing to record a single trade.

While disappointed with the initial response, Greg Boland, manager of the NZFOE's business development unit, said the newness of the new wholesale electricity market, which began on October 1, meant it could take some time for market participants to engage in futures hedging.
"I don't think there's a lack of interest," Boland said. "I think people just need to get their own board approvals and that sort of thing."
Six one-month futures contracts were launched on Monday. No trade occurred, although bid and ask prices were entered for the February contract.

Boland pointed out that there were still disputes between national grid operator Trans Power and South Island generators about who should foot the bill for transmission of electricity from the South to the North Island.
Furthermore, contractual obligations meant that generators could pass the buck to South Island electricity retailers.
That dispute would affect physical electricity prices, which would in turn affect the futures.

"They (market participants) believe there will be a wide spread in the futures because of that. They may not trade anyway because of that dispute, because they don't know how the physical (price) will be set," Boland said.
He said the uncertainty surrounding the new electricity market would resolve itself with time.

"I think the whole commoditisation of that market has meant a great deal of price risk and uncertainty, and I think the players will use the futures market once they become more familiar with it," he said.
